set.body:
Found by the PLS Neuro basis-set review on 2026-09-11 and checked numerically by an independent reviewer. Revision a3ee73b.

What the code does: bsplineBasis (HrfFunctions.scala:244-267) builds the full clamped basis, with knots 0 and span each repeated degree+1 times and interior knots at floor(span) * i / (m+1). It then drops the first (intercept) column to match R's splines::bs(intercept = FALSE).

Effects:
- Every basis function is 0 at onset, and the functions do not sum to one.
- A constant response is not in the span. For nBasis = 5 over 24 s, only 96.9% of a flat response's energy is captured.
- Whole-window mean weights for nBasis = 5 are 1/6, 1/4, 1/4, 1/6, 1/12, which sum to 11/12.
- A non-integer span gets an uneven last knot interval, because interior knots use floor(span).

Why it matters downstream: window means, a level-versus-shape split of responses, time-centring in a time-as-factor decomposition, and response-space (L2) metrics all assume, or are simplest with, a basis that contains the constant.

Decide: keep R parity as the default and add an intercept-inclusive (partition-of-unity) option, or make "starts at zero, excludes the constant" an explicit, documented property of the family.
set.title: B-spline basis drops its intercept spline, so it cannot represent a flat response
